Topic: New EU rules mean AI images need labelling from 2 August
Caption Notes: If you use AI to make images, video or posts for your business, new EU rules start on 2 August. Anything that looks real but isn't has to be clearly labelled, so people can tell at a glance. It applies if you sell to customers in the EU, even from the UK. Honestly, it's sensible practice anyway: just say when something is AI-made. Read the plain-English breakdown on ainofluff.co.uk.

Topic: The fake-boss voicemail scam every small business should know about
Caption Notes: Scammers can copy someone's voice from a short clip of them talking online. The trick going round: a voicemail that sounds exactly like your boss or a supplier, asking for an urgent payment. It sounds right, so people pay. The fix is boring and it works. Ring them back on the number you already have saved, never the one that called you. Follow @ainofluff for more plain-English AI safety.

Topic: OpenAI launches a ChatGPT programme built for small businesses
Caption Notes: OpenAI has launched a programme aimed at small businesses: online training, step-by-step guides, and ready-made links to tools you might already use, including Shopify, Slack, Dropbox and Intuit. One catch before you get your hopes up. The in-person AI academies are in the United States only, so from here it's the online bits or nothing. If you'd rather just have it in plain English, our guides do the same job. Browse the shop at ainofluff.co.uk/shop.html.

Topic: Android will have to let you pick a different AI assistant
Caption Notes: On Android, Google's own assistant gets the best access to your phone. The European Commission has told Google that has to change. Rival assistants like ChatGPT and Claude must get the same hooks, including voice activation and permission to actually do things inside your apps. It's an EU decision, so UK phones may follow along rather than change overnight. Worth knowing before your next upgrade. More plain-English AI news at ainofluff.co.uk.
